page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g6a.4xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with an AMD EPYC 7H12 processor running at a base clock speed of 2.6 GHz. The instance is configured with 16 dedicated vCPUs (8 physical cores with 2 threads per core) and 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage and network interfaces with a baseline bandwidth of 5 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks position this instance primarily in the average tier for multi-core operations. Multi-core CPU tests, such as stress-ng and Geekbench multi-core, show mid-range performance, while single-core CPU benchmarks fall into the lower percentiles. Memory performance is mixed; cached small-block read bandwidth is average, but uncached large-block read and write speeds are relatively weak. Standard workloads like gzip compression, bzip3 decompression, and static web serving throughput consistently register average results.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.g6a.4xlarge offers a balanced resource density for general-purpose workloads that do not require high-speed local storage or intensive single-core processing. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures stable performance without the throttling risks of burstable instances. This profile is suitable for multi-threaded applications, medium-scale web serving, database operations, and general-purpose enterprise applications that benefit from a balanced vCPU-to-memory ratio.
